prompt: A hexagonal patio tile has $6$ sides. What is the sum of its interior angles, in degrees?
hint: The total of the interior angles depends only on the number of sides. Recall the formula that uses the number of sides $n$.

hints.text: The total of the interior angles depends only on the number of sides. Recall the formula that uses the number of sides $n$.
The sum for a polygon with $n$ sides is $(n - 2) \times 180^\circ$. Put in $n = 6$ and work out $(6 - 2) \times 180$.
$4 \times 180 = 720$, so the interior angles add to $720^\circ$.

explanation: The interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides add to $(n - 2) \times 180^\circ$, because the polygon can be cut into $n - 2$ triangles.
A hexagon has $n = 6$, so it splits into $6 - 2 = 4$ triangles.
Each triangle contributes $180^\circ$, so the sum is $4 \times 180 = 720^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slice it into triangles
steps: Pick one corner of the hexagon and draw diagonals to every non-neighbor corner — you get exactly $4$ triangles.
Every triangle holds $180^\circ$, and together they cover the whole hexagon: $4 \times 180 = 720^\circ$. That is where the $n - 2$ comes from.
